text:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran an end-to-end nsys capture on staging to debug the perf regression for the 8-bit path. Timeline shows repeated host<->device memcpy bursts and a cluster of small dequant kernels that together dominate tail latency when KV cache hit-rate > 75%. Trace here: https://internal-traces/redwood/1918765432 (large)

mei: Can you paste the nsys command + env you used? Also which model + sequence distribution?

alex: nsys command I used:
```
nsys profile --output=trace_8bit_run --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none 
  --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=stop 
  --stats true --ffmpeg false 
  -- python -u run_infer.py --model redwood-8b-q --max-seq 1024 --batch-sampling "short:60%,med:30,long:10%"
```

env: BATCH_THRESHOLD=8, KV_CACHE=true, QUANT_PATH=int8-friendly

rohan: Two quick hypotheses: 1) batching heuristic is aggregating many short requests into one long micro-batch causing the kernel selector to pick the fallback kernels (host-side dequant step). 2) KV cache hits trigger additional host synchronizations because our KV-materialization logic pulls keys to host for dequant+copy before decoding.

sophie: Perf-bot just uploaded a summary: perf-bot: nsys capture complete — file=trace_8bit_run.qdrep size=1.2GB, top time buckets: memcpy H2D 23.4%, memcpy D2H 18.9%, small_dequant_kernel.* 19.1%, matmul_q8_cast 11.2%

mei: Oof. That small_dequant_kernel number is surprising — those kernels are meant to be fused into the matmul path for hot loops. Are we seeing version mismatch in the kernel registry? Check model build tags and the runtime's kernel index at startup logs.

alex: startup log excerpt:
```
2026-03-17T13:02:11.123Z INFO kernel_registry: loaded 312 kernels (q8: 42, q4: 28, fp8: 12)
2026-03-17T13:02:11.126Z DEBUG kernel_selector: registered policy=builtin_v2, fallback=host_dequant_v1
2026-03-17T13:02:11.127Z WARN kernel_selector: missing fused_dequant_matmul for model redwood-8b-q, using fallback
```

rohan: That WARN is the smoking gun. If fused_dequant_matmul is absent we fall back to a dequant->copy->matmul sequence. Why would it be missing? Probably build-time kernel pruning or a tag mismatch between compiled kernels and runtime kernel manifest.

mei: Quick repro plan: 1) re-run a short trace with environment KERNEL_FORCE_LIST set to include fused_dequant_matmul and disable automatic kernel pruning. 2) run with BATCH_THRESHOLD=1 to rule out batching heuristics. 3) run with KV_CACHE=false to see KV impact.

alex: Running step 1 now with:
```
export KERNEL_FORCE_LIST=fused_dequant_matmul,matmul_q8_cast
export KERNEL_PRUNING=0
BATCH_THRESHOLD=1 KV_CACHE=false 
nsys profile --output=trace_8bit_forced --trace=cuda,osrt -- python run_infer.py --model redwood-8b-q --batch 1 --max-seq 256
```

perf-bot: new capture uploaded: trace_8bit_forced.qdrep (240MB). Summary: memcpy H2D 5.3%, memcpy D2H 4.1%, fused_dequant_matmul 41.7%, matmul_q8_cast 19.0%, overhead runtime scheduling 7.4%

mei: Nice — that matches. With the fused kernel present we see a major drop in memcpy overhead and the heavy work moves into a fused op (good). So two action items: fix kernel registry mismatch and add a canary that ensures fused_dequant_matmul is present for INT8 runtime builds.

rohan: Also worth adding a micro-benchmark in the CI perf suite that exercises high KV hit-rate cases (simulate token reuse) and asserts memcpy ratio stays under X% for 8-bit path. I can open a PR for that.

alex: For immediate mitigation in staging, I'm going to pin the runtime to the build that includes the fused kernel and revert the pruning change. Rolling now.

sophie: And for long-term: consider reworking KV materialization so that dequant stays entirely on-device (avoid host round-trip) or introduce a lazy host-copy that only happens on eviction/serialization.

mei: One more thing — accuracy check. Did we run the eval harness after flipping fused kernel? Any numeric diffs between fused_dequant_matmul and the old host dequant?

alex: Ran a quick eval (1000 prompts): max ΔLL = 0.0012, mean ΔLL ~ 0.00005, top1 token diffs <0.2%. Looks safe, but we'll run full suite overnight.

rohan: Great. I'll file two tickets: (1) kernel-registry reconciliation + canary (2) CI micro-benchmark for KV-heavy 8-bit runs. Assign (1) to infra-ml, (2) to perf-tests.

sophie: TL;DR: regression caused by missing fused kernel + batching heuristics exposing host dequant overhead for high KV hit workloads. Fix = restore fused kernel, add guards, CI test, consider KV on-device strategy. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks team — I'll post deploy notes and attach the before/after flamegraphs in #eng-runtime once we have them.
